target: Establish a repeatable harness that submits source-linked formulas and inputs to a real Excel Desktop build and captures typed values and Excel error codes.
Record Excel version, update channel, calculation mode, and source workbook for each observation.
Start with high-risk existing profiles, including SORT/UNIQUE ordering and equality, array results, text limits, and date/financial boundaries.
Compare Python and Rust results to the Excel observation while retaining unsupported cases and undocumented behavior as explicit profiles.
Do not expand formula-family coverage until the first oracle batch is recorded and reviewed.
next_mutation.hypothesis: A real Excel oracle will separate implementation parity from Excel compatibility, resolve high-impact local profiles, and make later formula-family choices evidence-led.
reference_patterns: Use the existing source-linked JSONL case format and Python/Rust result APIs; capture Excel output as separate, versioned evidence. No third-party evaluator code or runtime dependency is required.
next_mutation.decision_support_advisory: Jev may assess whether an Excel source supports a narrow claim; it cannot validate observed calculation results or replace direct Excel execution and independent semantic review.
next_mutation.acceptance: Use a real Excel Desktop instance. Preserve formula, input, result type/value, error code, Excel version/channel, and run provenance. Re-run selected cases in Python and Rust; label each outcome as documented by Microsoft, observed in Excel, Formula Atlas profile, or unsupported. Do not claim broader compatibility than the observed case set.
